articles.title: Son Heung-min surpasses Cha Bum to become top goal scorer for South Korea
articles.description: Son Heung-min became South Korea's all-time leading scorer when his 59th goal helped the team beat Uzbekistan 2-0 in a friendly on Tuesday. The sixth-minute free kick moved Son past Cha Bum-kun's record of 58. Cha retired from international soccer after the 1986 World Cup. Oh Se-hun added a second goal on the hour as South Korea won comfortably at Mireu Stadium in Yongin, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) south of Seoul. Son also holds South Korea's appearance record with 151 caps. He made his international debut in 2010 and has played at four World Cups. The 34-year-old joined Los Angeles FC in 2025 after a decade with Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League. The win ended a mixed international break for South Korea and interim coach Robert Moreno. The team beat Ecuador 3-0, lost to Uruguay 4-1 and drew with Venezuela 0-0. South Korea and Uzbekistan are preparing for the 2027 Asian Cup which kicks off in Saudi Arabia on Jan. 7.

articles.title: Babar, Shaheen Dropped From Pakistan T20Is, Farhan Named Captain; Check Full ODI, T20I Squads
articles.description: Pakistan T20I, ODI Squad Announcement: Sahibzada Farhan has been appointed Pakistan’s new T20I captain as the Pakistan Cricket Board announced its squads for the upcoming white-ball assignments. Salman Ali Agha has been removed from the leadership role and omitted from the T20I squad for the series against Sri Lanka. The leadership change comes after Pakistan’s recent struggles in the shortest format. Farhan, who captained Pakistan at the 2026 Asian Games, will now take charge of the national T20I side. Sahibzada Farhan Takes Over T20I Captaincy Farhan led Pakistan during their run to the Asian Games final, where they eventually finished with a silver medal after losing to India in the gold-medal match. He will now begin his tenure as Pakistan’s T20I captain against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi. Salman Ali Agha has been left out of the T20I squad altogether, despite previously leading the side. His removal follows Pakistan’s underwhelming performances in recent major tournaments. The selectors have also made significant changes to the T20I group. Former captain Babar Azam, pace spearhead Shaheen Shah Afridi and fast bowler Haris Rauf have all been omitted from the T20I squad. However, the trio remain part of Pakistan’s plans in the 50-over format. Babar, Shaheen and Haris have been included in the ODI squad for the upcoming tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka. Shaheen will also continue as Pakistan’s ODI captain. Major Changes To Pakistan’s T20I squad Wicketkeeper-batter Usman Khan has also been left out of the T20I squad after a disappointing outing behind the stumps during the Asian Games final against India. There is also a maiden white-ball call-up for Razaullah, who recently made headlines during Pakistan’s third Test against England. The batter struck nine sixes in that match and has now earned selection across both white-ball squads. Pakistan will begin their three-match T20I series against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on October 9. The remaining matches will be played at the same venue on October 11 and 13. The T20I series will be followed by a seven-match ODI tri-series featuring Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka. Rawalpindi will host the first three matches before the tournament shifts to Lahore for the remaining league fixtures and the final. Pakistan Squad For T20Is And ODIS Pakistan's T20I Squad: Sahibzada Farhan (captain), Abdul Samad, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, Khawaja Nafay (wicketkeeper), Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saim Ayub, Shadab Khan and Sufiyan Moqim. Pakistan’s ODI squad: Shaheen Shah Afridi (captain), Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Babar Azam, Faheem Ashraf, Fakhar Zaman, Haris Rauf, Hasan Nawaz, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori (wicketkeeper), Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicketkeeper), Saim Ayub, Salman Ali Agha, Shadab Khan and Sufiyan Moqim.
